findings.evidence: Valid command/replay paths initialize Active or Disabled and validate assignable roles; the cited Unknown-role history is itself already uncertifiable before refresh. No real historical actor snapshot showing a newly lost valid certification was supplied. A production historical-state fixture plus the intended repair/rejection policy would settle this potential medium issue; do not invent a new public rejection.

The additional certification check really runs after the existing audit decoder. Normal production refresh already enforces the serialized bound before emission, and the retained oversized legacy fixture only demonstrates bounded parsing, not a resource failure. Moving the check before the audit decoder would add a new legacy-history rejection/skip policy; an uncommon low-impact concern does not justify that branch.

The new public-release verification recipe uses assert for its input, source/tag, workflow, artifact hash, package and signature-result gates. Inherited PYTHONOPTIMIZE or python -O removes them. Replace them with explicit failures and verify an optimized interpreter still refuses invalid input.

findings.claim: Generic artifact has no producing-attempt proof
findings.evidence: Tenants uploads generic release-candidate; the helper currently records the run latest run_attempt without identifying its producing job. Bind generic artifacts to an actual successful prepare-release job in an exact attempt, or refuse ambiguity; do not label a stale artifact as a later successful attempt.
